newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: CRICKET-ISRAEL REMAIN IN KL DESPITE MATCH INVASION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ISRAEL REMAIN IN KL DESPITE MATCH INVASION.

text.p: Israel is to continue playing in an International Cricket Council (ICC) tournament in Malaysia although a match was disrupted by Moslem fundamentalists, ICC officials said on Monday.
"The games are still continuing. We have plans for additional security," Satguna Singham, technical chairman for the ICC Trophy in Kuala Lumpur, told Reuters.

About 500 members of the Parti Islam se-Malaysia (PAS) invaded a match on Sunday which they thought was between Israel and Gibraltar. However, there was no incident as Canada and the Netherlands were scheduled to play on the ground, and officials abandoned the match.
Satguna said the organisers switched the venue of the Israeli game at the last minute after getting wind of the protest.
PAS had first protested against the presence of Israel in the tournament last week by marching past the Prime Minister's office in Kuala Lumpur, carrying placards and banners denouncing Israel.
Malaysia does not have any diplomatic ties with Israel and the Israeli cricket team's visit is the first by an Iareali sporting team, or any other official delegation.
ICC officials said Israel has two matches left to play.
"We will obviously do a last-minute switch of grounds to keep the games going," Satguna said, but declined to elaborate.

Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said last week his government had allowed the Israelis to compete in the tournament so that they could see "how different religious communities (in Malaysia) can live together without friction".
